newsitem.title: USA: ContiFinancial says FY97 earnings on track.
newsitem.headline: ContiFinancial says FY97 earnings on track.

text.p: Consumer and commercial finance company ContiFinancial Corp said on Tuesday it was on track to meet fiscal 1997 earnings targets, helped by strong growth in the asset-backed securities market.

"The company remains on track to achieve the earnings goals established when we went public this past February, while maintaining the capital strength, liquidity and portfolio quality that have always been our hallmark," ContiFinancial President and Chief Executive Officer James Moore told the first annual meeting of shareholders.
Moore was quoted as saying that the asset-backed securities market has grown at more than 25 percent a year since 1993 and ContiFinancial participated in that growth.

Through September 15, ContiFinancial had securitization volume of $1.8 billion, with $1.24 billion in home equity loans and $566 million from strategic alliance clients, the company said in a statement.
"Going forward, we are committed to maintaining a credit rating of at least BB+/Ba1 and the high level of liquidity we have achieved during the past year," Moore said.
"Over the longer term, we will work to eventually achieve investment grade ratings on our debt from several national ratings agencies," he told shareholders.

ContiFinancial's strategy was to focus on strong growth of mortgage originations while maintaining credit quality and low operating costs, Moore said. In fiscal 1997 through August, ContiMortgage originated about $1.3 billion, the company said, with expanding volume in the eastern United States.
Moorwe said ContiFinancial had also been successful in establishing new relationships with two California home equity companies and two sub-prime auto finance companies.
